correctness.rationale: The base-clique lower bound is proved by splitting each length-(n-2) prefix into its m final-coordinate cliques. A nonempty clique has >=r=m-k selected; if one is empty, every distinct adjacent clique has >=r+1 selected because its forced linking endpoint already sees an omitted outside neighbor. Hence its block contains at least (m-1)(r+1)=mr+k-1>=mr vertices; all cases n>=2, including boundary m=2 and k=1, are covered. The n=1 complete-graph case is independent. For the upper bound, an inversion-symmetric r-subset of Z/m selects exactly r vertices per clique and is constant across each possible linking edge. Therefore it dominates and has exactly k outside neighbors per selected vertex. The equality-case property for k>=2 follows from the strictly positive extra block cost. The standalone checker independently reconstructs coordinate adjacency and verifies 31 construction cases, 263568 enumerated candidate masks and 1225 cost identities. This is a complete all-parameter symbolic proof; the finite experiments are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The publicly accessible main primary text (arXiv:2610.01584v1) labels the exact full-parameter formula as Conjecture 12 and establishes only k=1 for arbitrary m and k=1,2 when m=3. The new result supplies a proof for all m>=2, 1<=k<=m-1, and a minimum-set rigidity corollary for k>=2. Semantic comparisons with the available published research records, related public records, and public literature found no stronger or equivalent theorem. The closest published-finding corpus hit treats complete multipartite rather than classical Sierpiński graphs. Search absence is not a uniqueness certificate, and accessible-abstract-only sources leave residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the exact, prominently stated Conjecture 12 in a recent primary graph-theory paper over the entire unbounded n,m,k range, beyond its proven k=1 and m=3 slices. The two-level clique charging lemma is a nontrivial needed extremal mechanism, and the inversion-symmetric residue construction works uniformly across all dimensions; an equality-case rigidity property follows. The mathematical value is the completion of a live natural family invariant, not finite benchmarking or a merely renamed result.
